title: Bioinformatics Analysis of Estrogen-Responsive Genes
author: Adam E. Handel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bnw9mfh6
materials: Register for the Genomic HyperBrowser ( https://hyperbrowser.uio.no/hb/ ).

steps.title: Prepare input data files
steps.instruction: Create two tab‑delimited files: (1) ChIP‑seq peaks with columns Chromosome, Start, Stop; (2) transcriptomic DEGs as ENSEMBL IDs (or convert other IDs using UCSC Table Browser: select clade, species, genome build, Genes and Gene Predictions group, appropriate Ensembl track, paste IDs, output selected fields). Use the demonstration datasets (ESR1 ChIP‑chip from Hurtado et al. and DEGs from Hah et al. thresholded at q < 0.05).

steps.title: Create Galaxy/Cistrome account
steps.instruction: Register at http://cistrome.org/ap/ to obtain access to the Galaxy/Genomic HyperBrowser tools.

steps.title: Upload ChIP‑seq and transcriptomic files
steps.instruction: In Galaxy/Genomic HyperBrowser choose Get Data > Upload files. For the ChIP‑seq file select file type “bed”; for the transcriptomic file select “txt”. Browse to each file, choose the correct genome build, and click Execute.

substeps.instruction: Upload the transcriptomic DEGs text file.

steps.title: Generate segment track from DEG IDs
steps.instruction: Use Generate Tracks > Generate segment track from gene IDs. Upload the list of ENSEMBL IDs as a comma‑separated value string. If the genome build differs from the one used for the ChIP‑seq data, lift the coordinates with Lift‑Over > Convert genomic coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Generate segment track from ENSEMBL IDs.
Optionally lift‑over to the desired genome build.

steps.title: Add 5 kb flanking regions
steps.instruction: Select Operate on Genomic Intervals > Get flanks. Choose the whole region, extend both upstream and downstream, set flank length to 5 kb, and click Execute.

steps.title: Concatenate and merge intervals
steps.instruction: First concatenate the original DEG intervals with the 5 kb flanking intervals using Operate on Genomic Intervals > Concatenate. Then merge overlapping segments with Operate on Genomic Intervals > Merge.

steps.title: Sanity‑check enrichment of ER binding
steps.instruction: Calculate enrichment of estrogen‑receptor (ER) binding sites within 5 kb of the merged DEG‑flank track. In the HyperBrowser select the enrichment tab, set Category to “Hypothesis testing”, choose “Overlap?”, select null model “Preserve segments (T2), segment lengths and inter‑segment gaps (T1); randomize positions (T1) (MC)”, set number of permutations to ~10 000 (for publication‑quality p‑values), keep Region and Scale at default (all chromosome arms), then run Descriptive statistics → Enrichment → Start analysis. Expect ~2.14‑fold enrichment with a significant p‑value.

substeps.instruction: Select tracks for ER binding and DEG‑flank intervals.
Configure hypothesis‑testing options and null model.

steps.title: Join DEGs with ER binding sites
steps.instruction: Use Operate on Genomic Intervals > Join. Select the merged DEG‑flank track and the ER‑binding track, then Execute to produce a table linking each DEG (±5 kb) with nearby ER sites.

steps.title: Export and filter results
steps.instruction: Paste the join output into a spreadsheet program, filter for unique gene IDs, and retain their associated ER‑binding sites.

steps.title: Re‑format data for BETA tool
steps.instruction: Ensure the ChIP‑seq file remains tab‑delimited Chromosome Start Stop. Prepare the transcriptomic file either as Cuffdiff/LIMMA output or as a tab‑delimited file with columns: gene ID, direction of change (e.g., T‑score), significance (e.g., FDR). Verify all entries are plain text or numeric; avoid spreadsheet auto‑formatting that converts numbers to dates, which can cause BETA to crash.

steps.title: Run BETA‑plus analysis
steps.instruction: In Galaxy choose Integrative Analysis > BETA‑plus: Binding and Expression Target prediction and motif analysis. Select the ChIP‑seq track, the transcriptomic track, the gene‑ID type (RefSeq or gene symbol), an output‑file prefix, the genome build, and the transcriptomic data type. If using a custom format, enter a comma‑separated list of column numbers for gene ID, expression direction, and significance (e.g., 1,2,3). Keep default settings for an initial run, then Execute.

substeps.instruction: Specify gene‑ID type and output prefix.
Set genome build and transcriptomic format.

steps.title: Inspect BETA output files
steps.instruction: Collect and review the following BETA results: (1) functional‑prediction graph (rank vs number of direct targets with p‑value), (2) tables of up‑regulated and down‑regulated direct targets with rank‑product scores, (3) lists of up‑ and down‑target associated peaks (distance and functional score), (4) motif‑analysis HTML file with top motifs and statistical scores plus detailed motif statistics, and (5) the BETA‑plus log containing input parameters and any errors.
